items.meaning: The ticker for Apple, a company that makes phones.
items.example: Buy 1 share of AAPL and you own a bit of Apple.

items.meaning: The ticker for Tesla, a car company.
items.example: TSLA is the ticker you type to find Tesla.

items.meaning: The ticker for Nvidia, a company that makes chips.
items.example: A chip is a small part in a phone. NVDA makes chips.

items.meaning: The ticker for an ETF that follows 500 big US companies.
items.example: One share of SPY gives you a bit of 500 companies.

items.meaning: The ticker for an ETF that follows 100 big tech companies.
items.example: One share of QQQ gives you a bit of 100 tech companies.

items.meaning: A box that holds many stocks and trades like one stock.
items.example: SPY is an ETF.

items.meaning: A way to buy a foreign stock in the US.
items.example: TSM is an ADR for a Taiwan company.

items.meaning: A big US exchange.
items.example: The NYSE is in New York City.

items.meaning: A big US exchange with many tech companies.
items.example: Apple trades on the Nasdaq.

items.meaning: The first time a company sells its stock to people.
items.example: The toy company had its IPO in May.

items.meaning: The boss of a company.
items.example: Mia is the CEO of a toy company.

items.meaning: The profit a company made for each share.
items.example: A company made $100 and has 50 shares. EPS is $2.

items.meaning: The price you pay for $1 of profit.
items.example: A P/E of 10 means $10 for each $1 of profit.

items.meaning: The price of one share times all the shares.
items.example: $10 times 1,000 shares is a market cap of $10,000.

items.meaning: The US group that makes rules to keep markets fair.
items.example: The SEC can fine a company that lies.

items.meaning: How much a country makes in a year.
items.example: When GDP goes up, a country grows.

items.meaning: The bank of the US. It helps set the cost of loans.
items.example: When the Fed acts, many stock prices can move.

items.meaning: The team in the Fed that votes on loan costs.
items.example: The FOMC meets 8 times a year.

items.meaning: A gauge of how fast prices are rising.
items.example: If CPI is up, things cost more than last year.

items.meaning: The highest price a stock has hit.
items.example: The stock hit an ATH of $50 today.

items.meaning: The lowest price a stock has hit.
items.example: The stock hit an ATL of $2 today.

items.meaning: The end of the trading day.
items.example: The EOD price is the last price of the day.

items.meaning: The time after the stock market closes for the day.
items.example: The news came out in AH, so the price moved.

items.meaning: The time before trading starts.
items.example: At 8 AM, PM prices show the first moves.

items.meaning: Stocks that trade away from the big exchanges.
items.example: A tiny company may trade OTC.

items.meaning: The top price a buyer will pay right now.
items.example: The bid is $10.

items.meaning: The low price a seller wants right now.
items.example: The ask is $10.05.

items.meaning: How many shares were bought and sold.
items.example: High vol means many trades.

items.meaning: How many shares trade in a day.
items.example: An ADV of 1 million shares means it trades a lot.

items.meaning: How busy it is now, next to most days.
items.example: An RVOL of 2 means twice the usual trades.

items.meaning: How far a price jumped from the last close to the open.
items.example: With a GAP% of 5, the price jumped 5 percent.

items.meaning: A number from 0 to 100. It shows how fast a price moved.
items.example: A high RSI means a price rose fast.

items.meaning: A tool that shows if a price move is gaining speed.
items.example: The MACD can show a price is losing speed.

items.meaning: The middle price of the day. Busy times count more.
items.example: Price over VWAP is high for the day.

items.meaning: A smooth line made from the last few prices.
items.example: A 20 SMA uses the last 20 candles.

items.meaning: A smooth line that cares more about new prices.
items.example: An EMA turns faster than an SMA.

items.meaning: How far a price moves in a normal day.
items.example: An ATR of $2 means it moves about $2 a day.

items.meaning: The four prices of one candle.
items.example: A candle shows its OHLC.

items.meaning: Reading up on a stock first.
items.example: Before I buy, I do DD on the company.

items.meaning: Hold a stock and do not sell.
items.example: She will HODL her shares for five years.

items.meaning: The fear that you will miss a big move.
items.example: The stock jumped, and FOMO made me want to buy.

items.meaning: A big bet on one stock.
items.example: A YOLO trade can win big, but it can lose big too.

items.meaning: An index of 500 big US companies.
items.example: If the S&P 500 is up, many big stocks rose that day.

items.meaning: An index of 30 big US companies.
items.example: The Dow went up when many of its 30 companies rose.

items.meaning: A website and app with charts.
items.example: I looked at AAPL on TV.

items.meaning: How long one candle lasts.
items.example: On the 5m TF, a candle lasts 5 min.

items.meaning: The OHLC prices and the volume.
items.example: OHLCV shows the prices and how busy it was.

items.meaning: Lines between a low and a high.
items.example: She drew a Fib from the low to the high.

items.meaning: The average of the last few candles.
items.example: The 20 MA is a smooth line.

items.meaning: Three lines around the price.
items.example: The BB got tight when prices were calm.

items.meaning: A number for how much the price swings.
items.example: A big SD means wild swings.
